albums.blurb: Hania Rani is a Polish pianist and composer, classically trained in Warsaw, who signed to Manchester's Gondwana Records — the label behind Portico Quartet and Mammal Hands — after founder Matthew Halsall heard her demos. Esja, named for a mountain overlooking Reykjavík, is her debut solo album: ten pieces for unaccompanied piano, recorded closely enough that the instrument's felt and hammer mechanics remain part of the sound. She later added voice and electronics on Home and Ghosts, but this record is where her catalogue begins.
albums.reception: Esja earned Rani four Fryderyk Awards, the Polish recording academy's honors, including Best Debut Album.

albums.blurb: Tyler's fifth studio album, produced entirely by himself, marked the turn from his Odd Future provocateur years toward the lush, jazz-chorded songwriting that has defined his work since. Guests include Frank Ocean, Rex Orange County, Kali Uchis, Steve Lacy and Lil Wayne, and the album's blend of rap verses with sung soul hooks set the template for IGOR and Call Me If You Get Lost, both of which won the Best Rap Album Grammy that this one was first nominated for.
albums.reception: Flower Boy debuted at No. 2 on the Billboard 200 and was nominated for Best Rap Album at the 2018 Grammy Awards.

albums.blurb: Jessica Pratt is a Los Angeles singer-songwriter who has released four albums of hushed, tape-warm folk since 2012. Here in the Pitch, released on Mexican Summer, is her fourth and most fully arranged: where her earlier records were mostly voice and nylon-string guitar, this one adds brushed percussion, bass, strings and organ in a 1960s California-pop mode, nine songs in a compact 27 minutes.
albums.reception: Pitchfork designated it Best New Music and ranked it No. 3 on its 50 best albums of 2024, while Stereogum placed it at No. 6 on its own year-end list.
